elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states: “No liquidated damages ... is payable by Customer under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalty under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states: “No ... penalty is payable by Customer under this Agreement.”

elements.element: If any liquidated amount is payable by Customer, it is payable only as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause expressly prohibits all liquidated damages payable by Customer; therefore, no non-termination liquidated amount is permitted.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because no liquidated damages, including an early-termination fee constituting liquidated damages, are payable by Customer.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position by expressly prohibiting both liquidated damages and penalties. It also satisfies the fallback as a more protective position: no early-termination fee or other liquidated amount is payable. However, the redline is not minimal because it also changes the payment grace period, adds “proper” and “undisputed” invoice conditions, creates a replacement interest remedy, and makes that remedy exclusive. The broad “Vendor's sole remedy” language may displace otherwise available collection, suspension, termination, or other remedies, so unrelated commercial rights are not clearly preserved.
